sentences.text: The case of the petitioners is that their land was acquired under the provisions of National Highways Act, 1956 and an award was declared on 31.01.2024.
The petitioners tried to challenge the same by filing a petition before the Commissioner of the Division.
However, their application was not entertained by the Commissioner on the ground that he has not been authorized to act as Arbitrator under Section 3-G(5) of the Act.

3. It is submitted by the petitioner, who appears in person that in such circumstances the petitioners have been left with no other alternative but to challenge the award by means of instant petition.

4. On 09.01.2025, the following order was passed:-
"1.

The petitioner, who appears in person, submits that he tried to avail the remedy of arbitration, as provided under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act but he was informed by the office of Commissioner that the Commissioner has not been assigned powers to arbitrate under the Act and therefore, he could not avail the said remedy.
2. Sri Rajive Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel seeks time to obtain instructions on the said aspect.

3. Put up tomorrow i.e. 10.01.2025 as fresh. "
5.

On matter being taken up today, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel has placed on record a gazette notification dated 30.06.2020, whereby power to act as Arbitrator under Section 3-G(5) in respect of District- Chitrakoot, has been conferred upon the District Magistrate- Chitrakoot.
6. In view of the same, it is open for the petitioners to approach the District Magistrate- Chitrakoot and avail the statutory remedy.
We are not inclined to examine the issues of facts in exercise of writ jurisdiction and particularly in view of availability of alternate statutory remedy.
7. The petition stands disposed of with the aforesaid liberty to the petitioners.
Order Date :- 10.1.2025
Shubham Arya (Anish Kumar Gupta, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.)
